newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs seen firmer if yen slides.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs seen firmer if yen slides.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures may be able to make more gains if the yen takes a further battering against other major currencies this week, dealer said on Wednesday.
Both instruments have risen over the last few days as the Japanese currency has slid against the dollar to around 111.80 to the dollar from around 110.80 at the end of last week.
"If the yen loses ground, we might well see Euroyen and JGB's climb further," said a Singapore-based Japanese dealer.
"And it looks like the yen is building for another move lower," he added.
Dealers said the market had a positive view of the current steady monetary policy of the Bank of Japan and expected a gradual recovery in the Japanese economy.
March Euroyen ended at 99.24, against a contract high of 99.25 hit early on Tuesday and a previous IMM close of 99.24.
Dealers said the contract had strong support around 99.18/.19 and would face upside resistance around 99.26/.28.
December JGBs slipped a little to settle at 122.10, after opening at 122.14.
"Most people expect the pay-roll data to be supportive but we may see a close lower before Friday's numbers come out," said the Singapore-based Japanese dealer.
March Eurodollars settled at 94.17, against a previous IMM close of 94.14. December ended at 94.28, against 94.26.
Support for the March contract was seen at around 94.10/.11, with resistance between 94.17/.20.
Eurodollar futures were also firm, rising across the board, particularly in forward months on a widespread confidence of minimal inflationary pressure in the United States.
"There is no sign whatsoever of U.S. inflation rising in the immediate term, wages are steady and we are unlikely to get any change in policy until after the U.S. election," said a dealer.
Most dealers said they were waiting for the U.S. non-farm pay-roll data due out on Friday to assess the direction of the Eurodollar market.
